02 Antipsychotics · class card

Atypical antipsychotics

second-generation antipsychotics · aripiprazole · asenapine · brexpiprazole · cariprazine · clozapine · iloperidone · lumateperone · lurasidone · olanzapine · paliperidone · quetiapine · risperidone · ziprasidone

Key point
  • Atypical antipsychotics block dopamine D2 and serotonin 2A receptors fewer extrapyramidal effects than typical drugs, more metabolic syndrome
  • Clozapine: resistant schizophrenia or suicide risk; severe neutropenia, myocarditis, seizures
  • Every antipsychotic: neuroleptic malignant syndrome (NMS) and a boxed warning for death in older adults with dementia
Drugs

Aripiprazole Abilify: partial agonist; akathisia, insomnia

Saphris: under the tongue AsenapineNo food for 10 minutes after the doseCan cause weight gain, extrapyramidal effectsCan cause numb mouth, dizziness

Brexpiprazole Rexulti: partial agonist

Cariprazine Vraylar: partial agonist; low metabolic risk

Clozapine Clozaril: best in resistant cases; drooling

Fanapt: QT, orthostasis IloperidoneTitrated over 4 days at the startTitration for the two risks: QT, orthostasis

Lumateperone Caplyta: low metabolic risk

Lurasidone Latuda: with food; low metabolic risk

Zyprexa: most weight gain; sedating; intramuscular for agitation Olanzapine with fluoxetineOlanzapine with fluoxetine treats bipolar I depressionOlanzapine with fluoxetine treats treatment-resistant depression

Invega: risperidone's metabolite PaliperidoneProlactin rise: high, as with risperidoneExtrapyramidal effects: high, as with risperidone

Quetiapine Seroquel: sedating, orthostatic; fewest extrapyramidal effects

Risperidone Risperdal: most prolactin and extrapyramidal effects

Ziprasidone Geodon: QT; least metabolic; with food

Mechanism

Limbic D2 block fewer positive symptoms; serotonin 2A block fewer extrapyramidal effects

Partial agonist at D2: an agonist where dopamine is low, an antagonist where it is high (aripiprazole, brexpiprazole, cariprazine) low-dose aripiprazole can lower prolactin

Tuberoinfundibular D2 block prolactin; histamine and alpha-1 block sedation, orthostasis

Uses

Schizophrenia, first line in newly diagnosed disease; clozapine after 2 failed trials or for suicide risk

Bipolar mania and depression

Add-on in depression Psychotic depressionMajor depressive disorder with psychotic featuresTreatment: antidepressant plus atypical antipsychotic

Parkinson disease psychosis: quetiapine, clozapine Other usesObsessive-compulsive disorder: risperidone as an add-onTourette syndrome: aripiprazoleAnorexia nervosa: olanzapineHuntington disease: atypical drugsSleep aid: low-dose quetiapine, often

Agitation: intramuscular olanzapine

Adverse effects

Metabolic: most clozapine, olanzapine, quetiapine; least Weight-neutral drugsWeight-neutral three: aripiprazole, lurasidone, ziprasidoneMnemonic: A, L, Z = first, middle and last letters of the alphabetWeight gain, lipids and glucose all riseMetformin with lifestyle measures can counter the gain

Prolactin: risperidone most; aripiprazole, quetiapine least SignsProlactin riseAmenorrhea, galactorrhea, gynecomastia and sexual dysfunction.

Erectile dysfunction with mild breast growth after starting an antipsychotic: gynecomastia points to prolactin rise from risperidone

Common wrong answers: alcohol, diabetic neuropathy, metformin, sertraline

: risperidone most, quetiapine and clozapine least; aripiprazole: akathisia Tardive dyskinesiaMost likely atypical cause: risperidoneLeast likely atypical cause: clozapine

QT: , quetiapineQT prolongationZiprasidone: QT prolongationRisperidone: also listed with ziprasidone for QT prolongation

Sedation: clozapine, quetiapine, olanzapine; orthostasis: clozapine most

Constipation, dry mouth: clozapine, olanzapine, quetiapine; on clozapine, up to ileus

Clozapine: severe neutropeniaAgranulocytosis; not dose dependent

If clozapine is planned, choose a baseline absolute neutrophil count (ANC), then counts throughout.

Clozapine: myocarditisFever, chest pain, fast pulse early in treatment

If it is suspected, choose stopping clozapine and a cardiac evaluation.

Generally no rechallenge afterward

Clozapine: seizuresHighest risk of the class; dose dependent

If there is a seizure disorder, choose avoiding clozapine where possible.

Neuroleptic malignant syndromeFever, lead-pipe rigidity, confusion; rarer than with typical drugs

If it is suspected, choose stopping the antipsychotic, then cooling and IV fluids.

Older adults with dementiaBoxed warning: more deaths, with stroke and heart attack Pneumonia riskMuch higher in older adults on antipsychotics

If an older adult's delirium agitation has cleared on an antipsychotic, choose stopping it and watching behavior.

Quetiapine kept after delirium agitation cleared: sleepy, stiff, shuffling; the reason for the drug has passed

Common wrong answers: months more then taper, split dose, risperidone, diazepam

Practice
  1. 27-year-old man started clozapine 3 weeks ago for treatment-resistant schizophrenia 2 days of fever, chest pain and shortness of breath pulse 124/min; no rigidity; thinking at his usual baseline troponin raised; absolute neutrophil count normal → Clozapine-induced myocarditis → most often within the first 2 months of clozapine; stop the drug and get a cardiac evaluation
  2. 38-year-old woman with schizophrenia switched to a new antipsychotic 2 weeks ago two brief spells of palpitations and lightheadedness no restlessness, stiffness or weight change electrocardiogram: corrected QT 510 ms, up from 440 ms → Ziprasidone → with quetiapine, it carries the greatest QT risk among atypical antipsychotics
  3. 24-year-old man with a first episode of schizophrenia started an antipsychotic 4 months ago constant hunger; has gained 9 kg now sleeps 11 hours a night; no tremor or restlessness fasting glucose 118 mg/dL; triglycerides raised → Olanzapine → olanzapine and clozapine carry the greatest metabolic risk, and both sedate
